intro: The README quick start connects to the Greenstand development database and needs a token from the engineering leads. The steps below use local containers instead, as CI does.
prerequisites: Node.js 20 and npm. CI tests on Node 20.
Docker, to run PostgreSQL with PostGIS and RabbitMQ.

steps.title: Start PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ
steps.text: These containers use the CI images. They are for local use only: PostgreSQL accepts connections without a password, and RabbitMQ accepts its default `guest` user from your machine. Use the `rabbitmq:3` image: RabbitMQ 4.1 and later refuse connections from amqplib 0.8, which this repo uses (`frame_max` 4096 is below the new minimum).

steps.title: Set the connection URLs
steps.text: The migrations, the tests, and the server read these variables. The service also connects to the legacy Treetracker database. For local work, point it at the same database, as CI does. Set the variables again in each new terminal.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.text: The API listens on http://localhost:3006 (for example, `/raw-captures`). The Swagger UI is at http://localhost:3006/docs/.
